power.look: a small dark pill with a coloured outline that pops in with a burst just above each person's head, reached by a dotted gold beam (dasharray 12 8) from Alex's glowing eyes
power.rule: a small number appears above each person's head, showing how many lives they have already lived

science.claim: Dr. Ian Stevenson documented 2,500+ cases of children reporting past-life memories at the University of Virginia.
science.source: Full script (approved); Stevenson, University of Virginia Division of Perceptual Studies
science.working: Real research cited in the full video; the 1-minute sample states the premise, the tick-down rule, and the Stevenson citation.

script.text: What if you could see something about other people that they'd never know you could see? Hey. Nice sweater. Oh, hey. Thanks.

I invented the lifesight detector. It's my own design. No one else has one. When I wear it, a small number appears above each person's head. A dark pill with a coloured outline, almost touching the top of their head. It shows how many lives they've already lived. Reincarnation. Call it what you will.
The number ticks down when a life is spent. Used up. Passed.
Look at Mr. Harwick, the history teacher. Seven lives. He's seen a lot. You've lived twelve times. That's incredible. Three lives, Jordan. You've got plenty left. I guess I'm due for a good one then.

Is this real? Is there actual evidence for reincarnation? The device I built is my own invention. It doesn't measure anything scientific. Dr. Ian Stevenson, a psychiatrist at the University of Virginia, documented over 2,500 cases of children worldwide who described detailed memories of previous personalities.
Part one. What happens at zero?
